result.summary: The intersection features sidewalks and traffic signals but lacks marked crosswalks and dedicated pedestrian signals, increasing exposure for people crossing. The pavement is in fair condition with visible cracking, and the land use is primarily commercial with street-level retail.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crosswalks
hazards.description: Lack of painted crosswalks at a signalized intersection reduces driver awareness of pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Across all legs of the intersection

hazards.name: Missing Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: Absence of walk/don't walk signals forces pedestrians to interpret vehicle lights, which may not allow sufficient crossing time.

hazards.name: Roadway Surface Degradation
hazards.description: Visible cracking and uneven pavement in the intersection area could cause tripping or difficulty for those with mobility aids.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground and center of the intersection

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style painted crosswalks to clearly define pedestrian space.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Add pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to all corners.

interventions.title: ADA Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install or upgrade curb ramps with truncated domes to improve accessibility.

result.summary: The image depicts a commercial intersection with basic pedestrian infrastructure, including sidewalks, a traffic signal, and marked transverse crosswalks. While a bike lane is present, the environment lacks high-visibility crossing treatments and features sightline obstructions from parked vehicles near the intersection.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles on the right side of the street are positioned very close to the crosswalk, potentially obscuring pedestrians from the view of approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the roadway, adjacent to the 7-Eleven

hazards.name: Low-Visibility Crosswalk
hazards.description: The crosswalk is marked with thin transverse lines which are less visible to motorists compared to high-visibility continental markings.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Install curb extensions to reduce the pedestrian crossing distance and prevent vehicles from parking too close to the intersection.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk Markings
interventions.description: Upgrade the existing transverse markings to continental or ladder-style markings to increase visibility for approaching drivers.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to improve sightlines between pedestrians and motorists.

result.summary: The street features continuous sidewalks on both sides but lacks marked pedestrian crossings or signals at the visible intersection. Parked vehicles along the curbs create significant visual obstructions for both drivers and pedestrians, potentially obscuring sightlines at crossing points.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crossing
hazards.description: The lack of a marked crosswalk at the intersection fails to designate a clear path for pedestrians or alert drivers to their presence.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Vehicles parked right up to the intersection corners block sightlines between pedestrians waiting to cross and approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Along both curbs near the foreground intersection

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install zebra-style crosswalk markings to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way and improve driver awareness.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces closest to the intersection to improve visibility for all road users.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct bulb-outs to shorten the crossing distance and physically prevent cars from parking too close to the corner.

result.summary: The image shows an urban intersection with basic pedestrian infrastructure including sidewalks and a marked transverse crosswalk. However, the environment lacks dedicated pedestrian signals and features significant visual obstructions from parked vehicles near the crossing.

hazards.description: Vehicles parked close to the intersection corner obstruct sightlines between pedestrians waiting to cross and approaching drivers.
